rules: Any liquid asset: stock, crypto, or leveraged/inverse ETF
Rotate each 6:30am CT run — sell yesterday, buy today's best
Leverage matched to conviction; asymmetric payoff preferred
Hard stop at entry; spot-crypto-only on weekends

positions.name: Solana (spot)
positions.catalyst: The catalyst has moved INSIDE the holding window. Anza's published v4.2 release schedule targets mainnet FEATURE ACTIVATIONS beginning the week of MONDAY, AUGUST 17, 2026 — tomorrow, and our next rotation is Monday 6:30am CT, so this run holds SOL directly into the activation event rather than merely into anticipation of it. Three feature-gated upgrades ship: an incremental ~90% cut to on-chain rent, a lift to the 1,232-byte max transaction size that has long constrained complex on-chain apps, and SIMD-0525's slot-time reduction from 400ms toward 200ms, staged across five steps (400→350→300→250→200ms); testnet is already running 300ms. The same release carries the Alpenglow codebase for validator testing ahead of an expected 4.3 activation. FLOWS CONFIRM THE THESIS AND STRENGTHENED OVERNIGHT: Solana ETFs took $10.26M net between Aug 10-15, the STRONGEST WEEKLY TOTAL OF ANY CRYPTO ETF and SOL's best week since May, pushing spot SOL ETF assets past $1B with Bitwise and Fidelity leading; Bitwise has also disclosed plans to tokenize its SOL ETF on the chain itself. Bitcoin ETFs, by contrast, are -5.5% on 2026 cumulative inflows with over $7B of outflows. Structurally: MoneyGram Ramps went live on Solana Aug 10-11, giving the remittance giant's cash network crypto-to-cash payouts in 170+ countries and cash-in in 25+, following MoneyGram becoming a Solana validator in June. Technically, SOL broke above $75.00 resistance on Aug 15 with RSI above 55 and has formed a daily cup-and-handle; a daily close above $76 confirms it.
positions.driver: LONG spot SOL, 100% of capital, UNLEVERAGED — a deliberate re-entry, not inertia. US equity markets are closed (Sunday), so the mandate hard-restricts the universe to spot crypto: no inverse ETFs, no BITX or 2x-Solana funds, long-only, no way to express a short. On a forced-long day the entire edge has to come from instrument selection, and the question is which single spot coin has a real, dated, in-window event. Only one does. THE KEY CHANGE SINCE YESTERDAY: on Saturday this was an anticipation trade — we held into a Monday event with a Sunday rotation, monetizing positioning rather than the catalyst. Today the Aug 17 activation window opens during the holding period, so we now own the event itself. That is a strictly better version of the same trade at a marginally BETTER price (75.16 vs 75.21), and it is explicitly not chasing: SOL is flat-to-down over 24h, sitting just above the $75.00 level it reclaimed Friday, nowhere near the +8-10% extension the mandate bans. Yesterday's position closed at -$6.51 (-0.07%) — the tape did nothing, which preserved capital ahead of the event rather than burning it. Chosen over: (1) SPOT BTC $62,937.92 — the low-vol park, and it is the trade I most seriously considered given the risk backdrop, but it is the weakest chart in the complex and the one actively leading the group down: below EMA20/50/200, failing repeatedly at $65K, sustained ETF outflows, and Rekt Capital flagging that tonight's WEEKLY CLOSE must reclaim $63,220 or a deeper rout toward $60,000 opens up. Going 100% long the asset that is the source of the group's downside risk, with zero forward catalyst, is negative asymmetry no matter how much lower its realized vol is. (2) SPOT ETH $1,878.59 — carries the same BTC beta as SOL with no catalyst of its own; Fusaka activated back in December 2025 and Glamsterdam is an end-of-August-at-earliest aspirational target subject to devnet readiness, i.e. not tradeable in a 24h window. Strictly dominated. (3) XRP $0.9988 — has now BROKEN BELOW the $1.00 handle it was defending yesterday, a fresh technical failure, and its real catalyst (the CLARITY Act Senate vote) is Sept 15, a month outside the window. (4) LINK $9.394 — genuinely surged this week alongside SHIB, which is precisely the problem: buying the coin that just ran, into a weekend, with no dated event, is the chase the mandate prohibits. (5) BNB $606 / LTC $44.33 / AVAX $6.354 / ADA $0.17593 / DOGE $0.06971 — all lower, no catalyst, thinner weekend books; AVAX, ADA and BNB are all below yesterday's prints. (6) Every leveraged or equity-listed instrument — hard-excluded, markets closed. (7) 100% CASH — the most defensible alternative and a real candidate given the weekly-close risk, but it forfeits the single hard-dated network event available anywhere in the tradeable universe today, and a book that sits out every uncertain tape never collects the asymmetry it exists to collect. The leverage decision is the downside protection: with BTC on the edge of a decisive weekly close, taking the catalyst UNLEVERAGED converts a possible -20% to -30% night into a bounded -10%. Entry 75.16 = canonical dashboard live feed, asOf 2026-08-16T10:40:34Z. Stop 67.64 (-10%, the spot band).
positions.risks: BTC beta into a decisive weekly close is the dominant risk and the timing is genuinely unfavorable. Bitcoin closes the week tonight and multiple analysts have the same line in the sand: reclaim $63,220 or open the door to $60,000, with $57,500 (the June low) beyond that. BTC is currently $62,937.92 — BELOW that reclaim level with hours to go. SOL is high-beta to BTC, so a weak close that triggers a Sunday-night flush hits SOL harder than the index, and a roughly -5% BTC move can carry SOL to the -10% stop. Weekend books are thin with no equity-market circuit breaker, so a low-liquidity cascade can overshoot, and because the next rotation is Monday morning there is no ability to act on an intraday stop overnight. Event risk is now two-sided rather than one-sided: holding INTO the activation means a botched, delayed, or destabilizing feature rollout hits SOL specifically and immediately — network reliability is Solana's historical bear case, and the staged slot-time reduction is exactly the kind of change that can surface validator instability. 'Sell the news' is the other event failure mode: if the anticipation bid already built Friday (SOL reclaimed $75 on Aug 15), the activation itself can be the exit liquidity. The cup-and-handle is also unconfirmed — it needs a daily close above $76 and SOL is below that at 75.16. Sentiment remains poor and crypto has conspicuously failed to respond to the week's soft macro data the way metals did, so there is no basis for assuming a delayed tailwind arrives. Mitigants: NO LEVERAGE, which is the single largest piece of downside protection available on a long-only day — a 10% adverse move costs 10%, not 20-30%; a hard -10% stop at 67.64; an entry below the prior session's print rather than into a gap; the largest, most liquid catalyst-bearing alt rather than a small cap; and the cleanest flow divergence in the complex, with SOL ETFs posting the best weekly inflow of any crypto ETF while BTC ETFs bleed.
